To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we have developed a prognostic model based on the expression of 10 proteins that is able to identify a subset of patients with stage II colon cancers who are at high risk for recurrence; (b) the 10 protein signature is superior to the current staging system for predicting recurrence in patients with stage II colorectal cancer, and (c) the 10 proteins can be measured by a simple, inexpensive immunohistochemical staining method.
The 5-year recurrence rate of stage II colon cancer patients is approximately 30%.

the 12-gene prognostic signature is an independent prognostic indicator in stage II colon cancer, and that patients with a high score on the prognostic signature have a 5-year recurrence rate of 30%, compared to a recurrence rate of 10% in patients with a low score on the signature.

there is no evidence that any particular prognostic factor is of clinical value for the individual patient.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prognostic subgroups are not associated with any specific molecular markers, nor do they correlate with any clinical parameters.

there are three major prognostic factors for patients with stage II colon cancer: 1) the presence of a high-risk histologic feature, 2) the presence of an adverse tumor biology, and 3) the absence of an adverse host biology.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the current staging system for colon cancer does not provide adequate prognostic information to determine whether patients with stage II colon cancer should be treated with adjuvant chemotherapy.
